# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary task is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
Games where the loop may pass freely through any eligible cell

- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must satisfy circle constraints (straight through white, turn at black)
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts by direction

### 1.2 Constrained Cell-Visit Loop
Games where specific cells impose strict entry/exit rules

- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop must go straight OR turn at ALL white circles within each bold-line area; avoids black circles
- **Mid-loop** — Black circles must be the midpoint of a straight segment of the loop
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each room once; must alternate between all-moon and all-sun rooms
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction constrained by wind arrows in black cells; cannot move against wind

### 1.3 Gate/Sequence Loop
Games where the loop must interact with structural elements in a defined order

- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all Gates in numbered sequence

---

## 2. REGION-DIVISION GAMES
*The primary task is to partition the grid into defined regions or blocks*

### 2.1 Division into Rectangles/Squares
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its cell count

### 2.2 Division into Polyominoes
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered blocks; each block's size equals its number; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per bold-line region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; all colored cells connected
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of black cells) so each bold-line region contains exactly two

### 2.3 Division into Specific Shapes
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows point toward the bend
- **Five Cells** — Divide into blocks of exactly five cells; numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell

### 2.4 Division into Paired/Symmetric Regions
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a white and gray area of identical shape/size
- **Nuritwin** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected globally

---

## 3. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*The primary task is to determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

### 3.1 Shading with Connectivity Rules
Games where shaded and/or unshaded cells must form specific connected structures

- **Nurikabe** — White cell islands defined by numbers; black cells form one connected wall; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Rooms have black-cell counts; black cells cannot touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicate numbers per row/column by shading; shaded cells cannot touch; white cells connected
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers count visible white cells in cross directions; black cells cannot touch; white cells connected
- **Usowan** — Numbers count adjacent black cells, but exactly one number per bold-line room is deliberately wrong

### 3.2 Shading with Shape Constraints
Games where shaded regions must conform to geometric rules

- **Choco Banana** — Black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must NOT be rectangles/squares
- **Shakashaka** — Place right-triangle shadings in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade whole rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles off it; no 2×2 uniformity

### 3.3 Shading with Gravity/Drop Rules
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per number clues; when all shaded cells "drop" downward, they fill exactly the bottom half

### 3.4 Shading with Sum/Count Clues
- **Kurotto** — Circles show the total count of black cells extending from them in all four directions
- **Tilepaint** — Whole tiles shaded or not; diagonal-number cells indicate black cell counts rightward/downward

---

## 4. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to place or deduce numbers in cells*

### 4.1 Latin-Square / Uniqueness Constraint
Games requiring unique numbers within defined scopes

- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box
- **Hitori** — (also in Shading) Eliminate duplicates per row/column by shading cells

### 4.2 Room-Based Number Sequences
Games where regions must contain specific sets of numbers

- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold-line room contains 1 through N (room size); duplicates in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N; arrow-black-cells indicate which neighbor holds the maximum value; same numbers in adjacent rooms cannot touch

### 4.3 Block-Size Encoding
Games where numbers describe the size of their own containing group

- **Fillomino** — (also in Region-Division) Numbers define block sizes
- **Chained Block** — Black cell blocks labeled by size; blocks must chain corner-to-corner; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

### 4.4 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill grid with numbers from a given list, placed horizontally or vertically like crossword entries

### 4.5 Snake/Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch sides; directional visibility rules from head apply

---

## 5. PATH / CONNECTION GAMES
*The primary task is to draw non-loop paths or connect elements*

### 5.1 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill all cells

### 5.2 Island/Node Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (1 or 2 per pair); all islands form one connected network; bridges cannot cross

### 5.3 Movement / Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally or vertically into their home country (one per region); paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles straight into gray areas; gray area numbers must match sum of entering circles

---

## 6. SYMBOL/MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to place non-numeric symbols or objects in cells*

### 6.1 Light/Visibility Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count

### 6.2 Directional Mark Filling
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers indicate the surplus of one mark over the other; marks cannot extend more than two cells in their perpendicular direction

### 6.3 Triangle/Shape Placement
- **Shakashaka** — (also in Shading) Place triangular shadings to create rectangular white spaces

### 6.4 Block/Domino Placement
- **Norinori** — (also in Region-Division) Place paired black squares within regions

---

## 7. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC GAMES
*Games combining two or more primary mechanics in inseparable ways*

### 7.1 Loop + Shading
- **Yajilin** — (also in Loop) Loop drawn while simultaneously determining black cell positions

### 7.2 Path + Shape-Building (Evolutionary)
- **Evolomino** — Draw squares in cells forming blocks; each successive block on an arrow's path adds one square to the previous block's shape without rotation/flipping

### 7.3 Division + Shading
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells so circled cells become promontories (one white neighbor); numbers indicate white-cell run length; white cells connected; no 2×2 uniformity

### 7.4 Loop + Region Constraint
- **Dotchi-Loop** — (also in Loop) Loop interacts with bold-line areas under uniform-behavior rules
- **Moon-or-Sun** — (also in Loop) Loop interacts with rooms under alternation rules

### 7.5 Path + Number Clues
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight runs) and draw lines from their tips; pencil numbers define line length; lines cannot cross

### 7.6 Shading + Maze
- **Nurimeizu** — (also in Shading) Shading creates walls; solution must yield a valid maze with shortest-path constraints

---
